column1: # seastones.cycles/1: Interdata 7/16 instruction execution times (SP-S4B, MACH-5)
# This is NOT a 7/16 timing table. No per-instruction table for the 7/16 itself could be read
# (docs/research/bitsavers-716-report.md). The values are the Interdata Model 74 times from
#   Interdata "New Series Models 74/70/80 User's Manual", publication 29-261R01 (Feb 1973),
#   Appendix 5 "Instruction Execution Times", printed pp. A5-1 to A5-2 (Model 74),
#   with class times from Table 1-1 of the same manual,
# used as a PROXY for the 7/16. Why the Model 74: its Table 1-1 class times (RR 1.5 us, RX 3.25 us,
# 1.0 us core) equal the only two 7/16 values read from the 7/16 Brochure (1973), LHR 1.5 us and
# LH 3.25 us, and both machines use 1.0 us core. The Model 70 is faster (RR 1.0 us).
# Every value was read from archive.org OCR text of the scan, not from the page image, and the
# OCR loses column alignment in parts of the table. Nick must check pp. A5-1 to A5-2 by eye
# before MACH-5 cites any value (SP-S4A sign-off). Until then the staff and About pages say
#   mnemonic  SIMH mnemonic (Interdata/id16_sys.c at the pin)
#   op        primary opcode byte, hex (Interdata/id16_cpu.c decrom[] index)
#   form      RR, SF (short form), RS, RX
#   base_ns   execution time in ns, no-branch case for branches, memory operand not indexed
#   per_n_ns  extra ns per unit of n (shift count, registers moved, bytes) or 0
#   taken_ns  time when the branch is taken, or 0 if not a branch
#   conf      read     = a legible row of the Model 74 table (or the 7/16 brochure)
#             unclear  = a value from the Model 74 table whose column could not be told apart
#             class    = the Model 74 Table 1-1 class time for that form (no per-row value read)
#             estimate = derived or borrowed (Model 70, or by rule), see note
# Indexing (RX with an index register) adds time on the Model 74; it is not modelled.
# Rows: all 113 instructions SIMH accepts on the 716 class (61 base, AL LM STM, 36 Model 5 group,
# 13 single-precision floating point). 8/16 and 8/16E opcodes are excluded.
